Shell execution tool

F01.shell-tool How commands run: shell, working directory, timeouts, output handling.

● supported

Value: `[toolset.bash] timeout_secs` sets the foreground bash command timeout (seconds, default `120`). The agent starts dev servers, builds and other long-running commands as background tasks on its own and collects their output; `x` kills a selected background task. The `!` shortcut is shell mode, on an empty prompt. Plan mode gates edit tools, not the shell: bash still follows permission mode.

Evidence:

  • E-grok-build-00082

    | `timeout_secs` | `[toolset.bash]` | seconds (default `120`) | Foreground bash command timeout. |

    Source: https://docs.x.ai/build/settings/reference.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

    The agent starts dev servers, builds, and other long-running commands as background tasks on its own, and collects their output when needed. Ask for it directly ("run the dev server in the background") or let the agent decide. In the scrollback, select a background task and press `x` to kill it.

Automatic compaction

F02.auto-compaction When and how history is summarized without a command.

● supported

Value: Grok auto-compacts as the context window fills. `[session] auto_compact_threshold_percent` (`0–100`, default `85`) compacts when context usage reaches that percent. `PreCompact` and `PostCompact` events cover conversation compaction runs. The `context` status item turns amber at the auto-compaction threshold, or at 80 percent when the agent reports none.

Evidence:

  • E-grok-build-00087

    | `auto_compact_threshold_percent` | `[session]` | `0–100` (default `85`) | Auto-compact when context usage reaches this percent. |

    Source: https://docs.x.ai/build/settings/reference.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

  • E-grok-build-00033

    `/compact [context]` compresses the conversation history to reclaim context window, with optional instructions about what to preserve. Grok also auto-compacts as the context window fills; check usage with `/context` or `/session-info`.

    Source: https://docs.x.ai/build/features/sessions.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

F03 Instruction files

Auto-loaded files

F03.auto-loaded-files File names loaded without being asked (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, rules).

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: Project rules load into context for every session in a directory tree. Per directory Grok reads `AGENTS.md`, `Agents.md`, `AGENT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Claude.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and every `*.md` in `.grok/rules/` (`.claude/rules/`, `.cursor/rules/` read for compatibility); gitignored files are skipped. Claude Code instruction files are read automatically.

Files ignored by `.gitignore` are skipped, which

    Source: https://docs.x.ai/build/features/project-rules.md; retrieved 2026-10-04; version not recorded; tier E1

Precedence and scoping

F03.precedence-scoping Which file wins and how directories nest.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: Grok loads rules in an order where deeper files take precedence on conflicts. Rules are read from every directory from the repo root down to the working directory (or only the working directory outside a git repo). A nested `AGENTS.md` scopes to its subtree, so a monorepo can carry different conventions per package. The `AGENTS.md` family is walked from cwd to the repo root.

Evidence:

Trust prompt

F04.trust-prompt The first-run or per-folder trust decision.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: Project hooks require trust before they run: the first time you open a repo with hooks, grant it with `/hooks-trust` or by launching with `--trust`. The decision is stored in `~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml` and covers project MCP and LSP servers too.

◐ partial

Output and blocking semantics

F06.output-blocking Exit codes or JSON that allow, deny, ask or modify.

◐ partial

Value: Exit code 0 allows, exit code 2 denies; only an explicit `deny` blocks. For passive events, stdout is ignored; exit 0 on success.

Limitation: `PreToolUse` is the only blocking event. Everything else, including timeouts, crashes and malformed output, is fail-open: the failure is recorded in the session but the tool call proceeds.

Worktree isolation

F14.worktree-isolation Git worktrees or equivalent per session or agent.

● supported ! unverified [unverified: no verified evidence record; settles by A tester pass of this supported cell against its cited quotes. It was outside the 30% verification sample.]

Value: A worktree session runs in an isolated copy of your repository, so parallel agents cannot overwrite each other's files. Plan mode

F19.plan-mode A read-only planning mode, and how it exits.

◐ partial

Value: In plan mode only the session plan file can be edited until you approve, independent of permission mode; the plan review is not skipped under auto or always-approve. The agent can enter plan mode on its own; leave with Shift+Tab when idle or q on the approval screen.

Limitation: Plan mode gates edit tools, not the shell — bash can still write via redirection. Reads, bash, and MCP still follow permission mode.

Auto-accept and autonomous modes

F19.autonomy-mode Modes that act without per-step approval.

● supported

Value: Auto uses a classifier to auto-approve safe tools; dangerous ones may still prompt. Always-approve skips permission prompts for tool calls (/always-approve, Shift+Tab or grok --always-approve). Deny rules and hooks still apply; auto and always-approve do not skip plan review.
